evidence.observation: "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population."
No CG1 acceptance case covers a second document's rows that violate a uniqueness, mandatory or value constraint satisfied by the first document's rows; the only CG-specific cases are for CG2 and CG3.

concerns.recommendation: State the outcome when the extended population fails validation: refuse the whole batch, which constraint and which rows are reported, and whether the preview shows the conflict before CAS. Add an acceptance pair: document A rows valid, document B adds a row conflicting on a uniqueness constraint, apply refused with the model bytes unchanged; and the same case without the conflict accepted.
concerns.title: CG1 does not define behavior when appended rows conflict with existing constraints

evidence.observation: "Preview row moves and role rewrites together, record merge, demotion, subtype or leave, recompute candidates after apply"
"After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row's original source." Only the successful path is checked; there is no failure or CAS-conflict case.

concerns.recommendation: Require that the row moves, role-reference rewrites and decision-log entry are published in one CAS, or none of them are. Add a falsifiable case: a stale CAS or a validation failure partway through the rewrite leaves the model, the population and the decision log unchanged, and no decision is recorded as applied.
concerns.title: Row/role rewrites are previewed together, but nothing requires the apply to be atomic

evidence.observation: "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold."
"Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply." No limits are named.

concerns.recommendation: Say what the threshold measures (candidate score floor, number of remaining groups, rounds, or reviewed groups). Add a hard round cap so the loop cannot run forever when a merge creates new similarity candidates. Add a case where a merge produces a new candidate group and the loop still stops at the cap, recording the counter and the stop reason.
concerns.title: Loop termination is defined only as 'the configured threshold', with no metric or round bound

evidence.observation: "shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans. Include two similarly named types with incompatible role players; the suggestion must carry evidence for review."
"Index singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns."

concerns.recommendation: Add a recall fixture: at least one planted duplicate per listed signal (singleton type, role-player shape, reading shape, name similarity, unit, counted noun) must each be grouped. Take the #339 reproduction's known duplicate set and assert it is found. Also add a negative case per signal that must not be grouped.
concerns.title: No criterion checks that candidate discovery finds the duplicates it claims to index

evidence.observation: "Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows."

concerns.recommendation: Define when two rows are the same row (exact tuple equality, or equality after normalization) and what a repeat does: attach an extra span to the existing row, refuse it, or no-op. Add cases for: the same row from the same span applied twice (idempotent), the same row from a different document (one row, two spans), and a near-duplicate that differs only by normalization.
concerns.title: Duplicate observations are counted but row identity and the attach/refuse rule are undefined

evidence.observation: "Append located rows to a locally owned fact"
"State validation order at each public boundary and test both sides of every refusal." The plan states no order for CG1 and names no ownership refusal.

concerns.recommendation: Define 'locally owned' (declared in this model, not imported or derived). Name the refusal for appending to a non-owned fact and state the CG1 validation order, e.g. ownership → span-in-document → population constraints → CAS. Test both sides of the ownership refusal.
concerns.title: 'Locally owned fact' and the CG1 validation order are not defined

evidence.observation: "Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338. The external option changes the atomic publication and summary contract and requires revising CG1."
"CG1 provides the canonical evidence representation for CG2 and CG3."

concerns.recommendation: Settle D1 before this plan is approved, or write CG1, CG2 and CG3 exit criteria for both storage options. The evidence representation, the CAS scope and CG3's atomic rewrite all depend on the choice.
concerns.title: The unresolved storage choice undermines the CG1 criterion and CG2/CG3's evidence dependency

evidence.observation: "After a rename or deletion validate all role references and locate every transferred row's original source."

concerns.recommendation: Add a case where merging two types moves rows that collide with the target's rows or break a uniqueness constraint after the move. Specify whether the merge is refused or the rows are deduplicated with both provenances kept.
concerns.title: Merging can produce duplicate or constraint-violating rows, and no case covers it

evidence.observation: "Emit stable candidate IDs"
"Vary identifiers, declaration order and input cardinality in the acceptance fixtures."

concerns.recommendation: Say what candidate IDs are derived from and which changes they must survive: declaration reordering, recomputation after an unrelated merge, and renaming a type that is not a group member. If IDs are derived from names, they change exactly when the fixtures vary identifiers.
concerns.title: The basis for stable candidate IDs is unspecified and may conflict with varying identifiers

evidence.observation: "accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log and verify that the declined group is not offered again unless its evidence changes."
"record merge, demotion, subtype or leave". 'decline' is not one of the recorded decisions.

concerns.recommendation: Align the vocabulary (decline vs leave). Define 'evidence changes' as a digest over member types, role players and cited spans. Bind each log entry to the model revision it was made against. Add the positive case: changed evidence re-offers the group.
concerns.title: Decision-log suppression rule and its vocabulary are underspecified

evidence.observation: "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply."
"name similarity". Pairwise comparison over all types, with no stated limit.

concerns.recommendation: Name the work limits (types indexed, pairwise comparisons, groups emitted, rows moved per apply). Name the counter recorded for each and the refusal when a limit is exceeded. Add a cardinality fixture that crosses each limit.
concerns.title: No work limits are named for discovery or apply

evidence.observation: "the closure replay must exercise two documents and an accepted merge."
"Milestone closure requires a replay across phases"

concerns.recommendation: State what the replay compares: a byte-identical model and population after re-running the decision log on the same inputs, the same candidate IDs, and every row's span still resolving to its document. Include a declined group and a duplicate observation in the replay.
concerns.title: The replay does not say what it compares or that it is deterministic

evidence.observation: "Growth policy currently directs later rows to open questions. Changing that public guidance belongs to CG1."

concerns.recommendation: Say whether appending is opt-in or becomes the default. If it becomes the default, pin the old open-questions behavior for callers who have not opted in, as §9's "pin the old behavior on unextended inputs" suggests.
concerns.title: Unclear whether later-row appends replace the open-questions default

response.summary: The plan names the right areas for #338 and #339, but the exit criteria are not yet falsifiable on the points the rubric stresses. For #338 it leaves open how appends that conflict with existing constraints are handled, how a row's identity is decided when the same observation repeats, and what makes a fact locally owned. For #339 it does not define the termination threshold or any work bound, does not say apply is atomic, does not test recall, and leaves stable IDs, decision-log binding and replay comparison undefined. Unresolved storage decision D1 also undermines the CG1 criterion and the evidence representation CG2 and CG3 depend on.
